label: Early original-phase input of one of {1, 2, y, d, 0, c, r}
explanation: Token detector that works only during the original phase (99% of mass) and fades with position. It fires when the input is one of 1, 2, y, d, 0, c (r is weaker), and the strongest firing comes from the first such token in the sequence. At t=0 it fires on every one of these tokens (precision 1.0). The firing rate drops from 23% of steps at t=0 to about 1% by t>=6. Later trigger tokens fire much less often, and repeats of an already-seen token rarely fire (in_first=1 holds 96% of mass). Magnitude is modulated by what came before: the top activations are y/1/2 at t=3-4 after l/e-heavy prefixes, which the predicate does not capture. It essentially never fires in the delimiter or copy phase, or on other letters. The predicate (trigger token at t<=1, or the first trigger token of the sequence) reaches dev F1 0.66 with mass recall 0.80, but many trigger tokens appearing later are false positives.
